text:
maya: Heads up — canary traffic isn't progressing past 10% in us-west-2. GitOps shows the splitter weights were updated in repo, but the live splitter keeps serving 10%. Anyone seen this before?
ops-bot: gitops-reconciler: started sync for routing/splitter @ abc123 (branch: release/canary) :gear:
sam: Did the reconcile succeed or fail? can you paste the reconcile log or `kubectl get events` from the routing namespace?
maya: Pasting relevant events (shortened):
```
$ kubectl get events -n routing --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp | tail -n 8
25m   Warning   FailedScheduling   pod/canary-xxx   0/8 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu, 3 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate
24m   Normal    Killing            pod/canary-xxx   Pod was evicted: The node was low on resource: memory.
23m   Warning   Unhealthy          pod/canary-xxx   Readiness probe failed: context deadline exceeded
```
sam: Looks like pods were evicted / pending due to GPU shortage and taints. Many canary endpoints aren't Ready. The canary controller will refuse to raise weights if < X% healthy.
liam: Cloud console shows two p4d nodes in us-west-2a were preempted unexpectedly ~30m ago. Provider reported quota exhaustion in that AZ.
nori: Also saw terraform drift for the nodepool size yesterday. `terraform plan` showed the desired_size changed back to 2 in staging config (we had 4 before):
```
# module.nodepool.aws_autoscaling_group.worker
  desired_capacity: 4 => 2 # (known after apply)
```
nori: If the planned nodepool is smaller than live, autoscaler may have scaled down and left us underprovisioned for GPU workloads.
sam: Why did GitOps reconcile succeed if endpoints were unhealthy? Shouldn't it have detected the readiness gate and paused the split change?
maya: GitOps applied the weight update, but the traffic-splitter controller has an internal safety check: it won't route >10% to a variant unless healthy endpoints >= 70%. The controller logs show: `canary-controller: desired_weight=30 but healthy_endpoints=1/8 -> holding at 10%`
frank: That check is good, but it leads to weird state: repo says 30% but live is 10%, so next reconcile thinks drift exists and re-applies, causing churn. We need a clearer signal in GitOps to reflect controller-enforced hold.
liam: Temporary mitigation: scale up nodepool to restore capacity, or drain non-critical GPU pods out of canary nodes. I can provision an emergency spot pool in the same AZ, but it costs $$$.
sam: Short-term steps I propose: 1) rollback splitter weight in repo to match live (set to 10%) to stop churn, 2) increase nodepool desired_capacity to 4 via terraform, 3) add a pre-sync check in our GitOps pipeline that verifies cluster has sufficient GPU capacity for target replica count.
nori: Agreed on pre-sync checks — we should run `kubectl get nodes -l accelerator=nvidia --no-headers | wc -l` and compare to desired replicas. Also add terraform drift gate to CI so nodepool size drift blocks rollouts.
maya: For immediate safety I patched the splitter to 0% (manual) to limit exposure while infra recovers: `kubectl patch traffic-splitter routing -p '{"spec":{"weights":{"canary":0}}}'` — that succeeded and traffic fell back.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollback initiated by maya at 2026-01-30T15:12:03Z — splitter.canary -> 0%
sam: Nice. I'll open PRs for 1) repo rollback to reflect 0% so GitOps stops flip-flopping, 2) terraform bump to desired_capacity=4, 3) a lightweight pre-sync health check step script.
frank: We should also consider changing the controller to surface a recommended repo state annotation when it holds a canary. e.g., `traffic-splitter.k8s.redwood/recommended-repo-weight: 10` so GitOps can reconcile to the controller's state instead of continuously reapplying.
liam: I'll stand up the temporary spot pool (p4d-spot-usw2a) and add node labels so canary gets scheduled there. ETA ~25m. Monitor costs.
nori: Also filing infra follow-up: INFRA-2319 — investigate why autoscaler allowed scale-down below the planned min, and why our drift detection didn't block the release.
maya: Thanks all. Monitoring LB / error budget and canary metrics. Please ping here when the nodes are up or if PRs land.
sam: PRs: #482 (repo rollback), #483 (terraform capacity bump), #484 (gitops pre-sync check) — linking in case you want to review.
frank: Postmortem action items: 1) add pre-rollout capacity check, 2) have controller annotate repo recommended weight, 3) strengthen terraform drift alerts, 4) run chaos test for node eviction scenarios.
maya: Closing loop: splitter is stable at 0%, canary pods are Pending until nodepool scales. Will re-run canary once healthy endpoints >= 70%.
